root_cause: Daily historical peak/heatmap prewarm sustained CPU load in API process; Polars 32-thread execution used roughly four times the CPU time of 4-thread execution on sampled peak calculations, with no wall-time advantage.

isolated_comparison.sample: 3 historical code/date pairs, two runs per thread setting; raw calculation cache=None; DuckDB=4 threads; cProfile enabled; filesystem caches not cleared

secondary_findings: Peak computation executed 158 Polars collect calls per sample day.
Prewarm presence checks parse and validate full ask/bid/depth cache bodies; sampled checks read 1.65-1.71 MB and took about 10-12 ms.
Live GC warnings of 3-second pauses occurred during prewarm; last warning at 23:09:58 before prewarm completion. GC counts are global to the API process and do not establish per-task attribution.
limitations: No live stack profiler was attached: ptrace requires unavailable sudo authentication.
Live before/after was a natural job completion, not a randomized experiment; other laptop activity was not controlled.
Isolated profiles establish sampled function cost and output equality, not exact CPU share for every historical date.
No fan RPM or thermal-throttling telemetry available; no hardware cooling fault conclusion.
CPU time across threads is not measured electrical energy.
recommended_priority: Bound CPU parallelism for prewarm, preferably in a separate worker so foreground chart requests retain their current settings.
Add time/CPU budget and pacing to prewarm; current limit is only the number of newly warmed items.
Optimize cache presence checks without bypassing freshness/version validation.
Do not prioritize reducing capture concurrency based on this incident: 10 captures continued after heat and main CPU fell.
